name: Inactive Room Assigned to Future Stay
natural_language: No future reservation may reference a room that is inactive or decommissioned.

population.description: Non-cancelled reservations arriving from today onward. The room master is joined as a reference, one call for the whole property, rather than being queried per stay.

minihotel.call_cost: 1 + R: one population call plus one room-master call, whatever the number of stays. v1's query started from getRooms and asked the engine to cut a rooms response into stays, which it cannot do - the join it described in prose is now declared as a reference.

predicates.note: The assigned room still exists in the room master.

execution.rationale: Type C, and the architecture doc's own worked example for this mode. A room can be decommissioned with no reservation event emitted, so events alone would miss it.

freshness_requirement.rationale: Concerns future stays; there is time to react. The doc explicitly rates this class low-urgency.

unknown_conditions.when: a room is absent from getRooms
unknown_conditions.reason: absence is the signal, but it cannot be distinguished from a room that was never visible to this integration user. Note R6 was investigated and unmapped rooms ARE still returned, so this is unlikely - but it is not guaranteed for every tenant.

caveats: MiniHotel has no explicit active/inactive flag. 'Inactive' is inferred from absence from the room master or presence of a closed window.
Room numbers are not always numeric - one sandbox room is named 'Nemanja'. Do not assume integer keys.
